candidates: When optimizer or dynamics classes store open file handles or trajectory objects as persistent instance attributes, flag this as a resource-management smell. The preferred pattern is to store only the file path or configuration on the object, open the file within the narrowest applicable scope (e.g., inside `irun` via a context manager), and pass the open stream explicitly to logging/writing helpers rather than stashing it on `self`.

When a change causes logfiles or trajectory files to be opened and closed on every optimizer or MD step (rather than held open for the duration of a run), flag the potential performance regression for fast-running simulations such as classical MD with fast calculators. Verify that callers can opt into better I/O performance by passing a pre-opened file object instead of a path string, and confirm this escape hatch is documented. For ASE in particular, consider whether known downstream heavy users of the optimizer infrastructure (e.g., janus-core, asap3, fhi-vibes) are affected and whether their maintainers should be notified.
